name: Avestan
blurb: Sacred language of the Zoroastrian scriptures, close kin of Old Persian. Its pairi-daēza, a walled garden, is the Iranian word behind paradise.

name: Min Nan (Hokkien)
blurb: Language of Fujian's seafaring traders. Its tê gave English tea, and its kê-tsiap probably gave ketchup.

name: Malayalam
blurb: Language of Kerala on India's spice coast, where Portuguese traders first picked up the word mango.

name: Ilocano
blurb: Language of northern Luzon in the Philippines; probably the source of yo-yo.

name: Haitian Creole
blurb: A French-based creole with deep West and Central African roots; gave English zombie.

name: Serbo-Croatian
blurb: South Slavic language; its papar, pepper, became Hungarian paprika.

name: Tahitian
blurb: Polynesian language of Tahiti; Captain Cook's crew brought home its tatau as tattoo.

name: Tongan
blurb: Polynesian language of Tonga; gave English taboo (tapu).
